name: Arke Telekom
evidence: Headline: Arke Telekom lands €1M from ACT Venture Partners to advance drone communications

Summary: Arke Telekom, a company developing defence andcommunications technologies, has secured €1 million in funding from ACT VenturePartners, a venture capital firm focused on deeptech investments. The compa...

assessment.whatTheyDo: Ankara-based defence communications company building ArkeLink, a jam-resistant, GNSS-independent software-defined-radio mesh network for tactical drones, alongside military waveform consulting and simulation work.
concerns: Defence and weapons systems is an explicit anti-interest. The product is military drone communications sold to defence primes.
Headquartered in Ankara, Türkiye, so visa, relocation or time-zone gap makes it materially harder for a US-based person to join.
The €1M round is below the preferred $2M minimum.
No open roles are listed on the careers page. Applications go through LinkedIn, with no sign of senior or staff engineering hiring.
Revenue looks consultancy-driven (waveform consulting, simulation tools, automotive software) rather than product-led.
No US presence or remote-friendly hiring found.
assessment.rationale: The company is real and technically substantive (SDR, mesh networking, waveform design), but it is a defence company, which the person actively avoids. It is also based in Türkiye, with a small round and no visible open roles. Strong embedded and radio depth is outweighed by the anti-theme and geography.
assessment.summary: Arke Telekom is an Ankara-based defence-communications firm, apparently founded around 2020 or earlier given its NATO facility clearance and ASELSAN supplier listing. It builds ArkeLink, a frequency-hopping mesh radio for jamming-resistant drone comms. It raised €1M from ACT Venture Partners and was selected for NATO DIANA. It is technically credible but defence-focused and non-US, so a poor fit for this person.
assessment.product: ArkeLink: a GNSS-independent, frequency-hopping, self-healing mesh communication system for tactical UAVs. The company also offers waveform design (including UHF SATCOM), military waveform consulting, and simulation/emulation tools (ModSatSim, TSim). It sells to defence customers and has some automotive software work.
assessment.team: Co-founders are Dr. Saygun Önay (CEO) and Barış Karadeniz (CTO), per tech.eu. No further backgrounds were found, and the company's team page has no detail.
assessment.funding: €1M (about $1.0M) announced 2026-10-22 from ACT Venture Partners, a deeptech VC. No other investors or earlier rounds were found. The company was selected for the NATO DIANA accelerator.
redFlags: Defence and weapons-adjacent business
Non-US headquarters (Türkiye)
Sub-minimum round size
No visible engineering hiring
Customers are mainly Turkish defence primes (Aselsan, Meteksan, Karel), which suggests concentration
greenFlags: Real shipping product (ArkeLink) with defence-prime references
Deep RF and embedded technical focus
Technical founders (PhD CEO, CTO)
NATO DIANA selection and NATO facility security clearance
Small team, so engineers likely have high leverage

name: Mach9
evidence: Headline: Mach9 raises $34M after pivoting to AI CAD software
Summary: The startup initially set out to build better, faster, and cheaper surveying hardware in 2021.

assessment.whatTheyDo: Mach9 builds AI-native CAD software that turns LiDAR scans and imagery into draft survey drawings (curbs, signs, poles, lane markings) for surveyors and civil engineers to review and edit.
matchedInterests: Applied AI in a specific vertical (legal, health, finance, logistics)
concerns: Go-to-market expansion is the stated use of the new funds, so hiring may lean toward sales rather than senior engineering.
The only engineering openings I found were an early-career ML Engineer role and a mid-level SDET role. I found no senior or staff roles.
Headquarters is inferred from job-board listings and not confirmed on the company's own site.
Customer traction (about 100 beta customers, 2,500+ projects) and the 10x faster / one-fifth cost claims come from the company and are unverified.
Civil engineering and surveying is a niche market with slow-moving, conservative buyers.
The company pivoted from hardware, so the software product is still young.
assessment.rationale: This is a real vertical-AI product with technical founders from CMU robotics and 3D perception, credible backers (First Round, Bessemer) and early customer usage. The $34M Series A is a sensible size for a company with a shipped product. The score is held below the strong-match band because there are no senior engineering roles, the market is niche, and the claims are not independently verified.
assessment.summary: Mach9 started in 2021 as Mach9 Robotics building surveying hardware. It pivoted to AI-native CAD software for surveyors and civil engineers. It raised a $34M Series A in October 2026, co-led by First Round Capital and Bessemer, bringing total funding to about $49M. It is a real product with early traction in a niche vertical, and it looks worth a look for an engineer who likes 3D perception and vertical AI.
assessment.product: Digital Surveyor, a browser-based 3D CAD platform. It ingests LiDAR and imagery, uses AI to extract features and propose a first-draft drawing, and the surveyor edits it. Pricing is usage-based, per mile of road or acre surveyed. Survey data stays in the platform as a system of record.
assessment.team: Four co-founders who met at Carnegie Mellon University while building robots: Alexander Baikovitz (CEO), Haowen Shi, Michael Mong and Zachary Sussman. Their robotics work gave them 3D perception expertise. I found no team size.
assessment.funding: $34M Series A announced 2026-10-21, co-led by First Round Capital and Bessemer Venture Partners, with Prudence and Quiet Capital participating. Total funding is reported as about $49M.
redFlags: Hiring emphasis appears to be go-to-market after the raise.
Engineering roles found were junior to mid-level only.
Traction numbers are self-reported.
greenFlags: Technical founders with robotics and 3D perception backgrounds.
Shipped product with about 100 beta customers on 2,500+ projects.
Reasonably sized Series A from top-tier investors, not a very large seed.
The company chose to drop hardware and focus on software.
Usage-based pricing and a system-of-record data position give it some defensibility beyond a thin wrapper.
The company is hiring ML engineers working on proprietary perception models.
